newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine plans to up Russian gas transit to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans to up Russian gas transit to Europe.

text.p: Ukraine's top energy official said on Thursday that the country, already the most important transit point for Russian gas supplies to Europe, would seek to increase transit volumes by nearly a fifth by 2005.

"The programme of development of gas pipelines foresees increasing the gas transit from Russia to Europe through Ukrainian territory to 147-150 billion cubic meters (bcm) annually by year 2005," Bohdan Klyuk, head of the Ukrgazprom share-holding company, told reporters.
But Klyuk also expressed concern over Russian plans to construct an alternative gas pipeline for supplies to Europe which would avoid Ukrainian territory.
This year Ukraine is due to pump 126-129 bcm of Russian gas to the West compared to last year's 117 bcm.
Klyuk said the increase would mostly be accomplished with more Russian gas being sent to Turkey via Ukraine and Romania.

Kiev and Moscow agreed last year to set a tariff of $1.75 per one hundred km (62 miles) per 1,000 cubic metres of Russian gas carried via Ukraine -- but Russia pays the fees in gas, with about 32 bcm of gas as payment this year.
Altogether Ukraine consumes 86 bcm each year -- including 18 bcm from domestic output -- with the rest imported from the Central Asian states of Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
Klyuk said Ukraine was worried about Russian gas monopoly Gazprom's plans to build a pipeline from the remote Yamal gas field to Europe via Ukraine's northern neighbour Belarus and Poland.
The $40 billion project, inaugurated last year, foresees building a twin pipeline with annual transit capacity of 60 bcm, but the scheme suffers from a lack of financing.
"There are grounds for worry," Klyuk said. "Western investors have been thinking about whether to put money into the new project, or into modernisation of our old pipeline."
